@graph.description: Under NITA, Access — a popular fare pilot that enables Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) recipients to ride Metra at a reduced fare — expanded to CTA and Pace on October 1. The NITA Board of Directors met for the first time on September 10 and hit the ground running by approving this Access Pilot Program expansion. With the Board’s action to expand the program, those who qualify can now ride CTA and Pace at 50 percent off, making CTA bus rides $1.10 and L rides $1.25, and Pace bus rides only $1. “By making Access available across CTA, Metra and Pace, we’re turning a successful pilot into a regional benefit and making transit more equitable and affordable for riders who need it most.” Current Access riders There are currently 9,000 active Access permits being used on Metra. One Metra rider enrolled in the Access Pilot Program, Tiana Love of Chicago, said she and her family ride Metra much more often now that she’s able to purchase tickets at a reduced fare.
